page.layout: Top: woodcut headpiece ornament. Below it, centred title block in capitals: "ETHICA CONTRACTA: PROOEMIVM ETHICÆ." One column of running text below, opening with a large woodcut initial H. Page number top right. Signature "A" centred at the foot. No running head, no marginal notes.

main_text.head: ETHICA CONTRACTA: PROOEMIVM ETHICÆ.
main_text.p: HOc Proœmio nomen, definitio, objectum, causæ, & divisio Ethicæ explicantur.

Nomen Ethicæ derivatur à græco ἦθος[?] quod significat mores, eo quòd de moribus tractet: unde Ethica dicitur Philosophia moralis: per mores autem intelligimus, non consuetudines alicujus regionis, sed actiones humanas.

Ethica definitur Habitus directivus operationum voluntatis ad bonum honestum: quia tradit præcepta, quibus dirigitur voluntas in suis operationibus honestè exercendis. Per directionem actionum voluntatis distinguitur Ethica à Logicâ, quæ dirigit tantùm operationes mentis. Per actiones autem voluntatis intelligitur tam elicitas quàm imperatas, idque in communi; ut distinguatur Ethica à Prudentia, quæ versatur circa actiones voluntatis in particulari, addendo vel detrahendo præceptis communibus Ethicæ, pro aliis circunstantiis loci, temporis, & personarum.

Objectum materiale Ethicæ est actio voluntatis, seu actio humana; quia talis actio explicatur in Ethicâ; Objectum verò formale est rectitudo moralis in actionem humanam inducenda; quæ explicatur his verbis, quatenus dirigenda ad bonum honestum. Nam actio humana eo tantùm modo consideratur in Ethicâ; in Physicâ verò consideratur; prout est actio compositi naturalis, scilicet hominis. Objectum formale sub quo, seu ratio formalis sub qua, est dirigibilitas ad bonum honestum; quia talis dirigibilitas seu capacitas accipiendi rectitudinem moralem, est conditio requisita in objecto materiali Ethicæ. Denique

page.notes: The initial H is a woodcut letter, joined to "Oc" as "HOc". The Greek word after "à" (ἦθος) is hard to read at this scan resolution; the reading is uncertain and marked [?]. Typeset s rendered as s throughout. Visible printing irregularities (for example "Ethicæ.est", "Objectum materiale Ethicæ .est") are reproduced as spaced in the print.
